A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveMoE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices. Their shared framework and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization and additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bench2Drive evaluations of Drive-π0 and DriveMoE, component and expert-count ablations, camera-selection experiments, and router accuracies.

after.justification: v2 reports original Bench2Drive results and expanded ablations, plus nuScenes planning results and computational-cost measurements in the supplement.

M1.justification: v1 presents one supervised Action MoE. v2 Section 2.4 introduces separately specified and evaluated token-level and trajectory-level alternatives: independent token routing versus routing after averaging the token sequence, with trajectory routing designated as default. This substantially extends the routing design while retaining Vision MoE and the overall two-stage framework; it does not establish that every retained result used a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix 10 adds actual open-loop planning evaluation on nuScenes, extending coverage from CARLA/Bench2Drive simulation to real-world driving data. Bench2Drive's 220 routes, 1,000-clip base dataset, and five driving-skill categories remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds DriveMamba-L and Raw2Drive to the Bench2Drive comparison while retaining the earlier external comparators. The new nuScenes comparison uses UniAD and VAD-Base, alongside Drive-π0; these should not all be counted as entirely new baseline families.

E3.justification: The reported training recipe changes from 10+5 epochs and effective batch size 1,024 to 12+6 epochs and batch size 128. Vision/action router loss weights change from 0.05/0.03 to 10/10 in stage one and from 0.05/0.025 to 5/5 in stage two. Added experiments introduce further camera/expert configurations, resource measurements, and horizon-wise nuScenes L2/collision evaluation. These are documented setting changes, without establishing that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands the camera ablation to multiple fixed-view combinations with latency and memory measurements, adds a controlled token-versus-trajectory routing comparison, and tests action supervision and shared-expert counts. Earlier component-removal, non-shared-expert-count, and router-accuracy analyses are retained under new table numbers. The additions test substantial previously unexamined design and efficiency questions.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that results are averaged over three runs; v1 gives no corresponding repeated-run count. Neither version reports seeds, standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This establishes added reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises Drive-π0's driving score from 60.45 to 55.85 and average L2 from 0.56 to 1.13. The main DriveMoE row retains 74.22 driving score and 48.64% success but changes L2 from 0.38 to 1.01. Baseline ability scores and fixed-camera results also change, while routing variants, expanded ablations, nuScenes outcomes, and resource results are added. Given revised training settings, these are revised reported results rather than established same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: v1 names the flow-matching loss without defining it. v2 Appendix 6 adds Equation 7 and specifies the conditional expectation, noisy-action interpolation, and target vector field. This adds mathematical specification of an existing objective, rather than a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2's abstract newly presents the implementation and investigation of two action-routing styles as a contribution. The principal claims about adapting π0, combining vision and action MoE, handling rare behaviors, and achieving Bench2Drive state-of-the-art performance remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting additional fixed views to convergence difficulty, nuScenes results to real-world generalization, and computational cost to extra views and expert activation. Appendix 8 adds unsupervised-selection and distillation directions. Although the dedicated limitations/social-impact section disappears, the important expert-load-imbalance caveat remains in the main text.

D1.justification: v2 substantially revises the numerical training recipe, specifies the existing flow-matching objective, discloses a rear-view annotation fallback, and adds parameter counts, FLOPs, memory, latency, and GPU-hour costs. Implementation details move to Appendix 7. The explicit code/model-release promise and supplementary-movie pointer disappear, although the project-page link remains; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially refreshes the research context through newer driving/VLA citations, expanded discussion of DriveGPT-4 and DriveLM, new treatments of LeapAD and SimLingo, and connections to DySS, LightVLA, and distillation. Several earlier trajectory/perception references disappear. This broadens the substantive positioning beyond merely moving Related Work to the supplement.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, splits Action MoE into dedicated routing subsections, moves Related Work and Implementation Details into the supplement, and reorganizes the experimental narrative. The supplement receives a new structure covering the loss, implementation, discussion, annotations, nuScenes, and efficiency. These are substantial organizational changes beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document to two columns, redraws the conceptual and architecture figures, and adds a separate trajectory-router diagram. The camera table becomes a view-selection matrix with resource columns, the expert table gains shared-expert and supervision columns, and new routing, nuScenes, and cost tables appear. Existing tables are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The new routing controls, efficiency evidence, and nuScenes evaluation strengthen the paper's empirical breadth. However, v2 introduces material conflicts between tables and retained claims: Table 2 gives Raw2Drive higher success than DriveMoE (50.24% versus 48.64%), and DriveMoE's revised L2 of 1.01 is no longer lowest, although Section 3.2 still claims both distinctions. Its retained 22.8% driving-score improvement also conflicts with the revised baseline, which implies approximately 32.9%. These gains and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
